rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AT LEAST ONE (1) SPECIAL EDUCATION (SPED) CENTER FOR EACH SCHOOL DIVISION AND AT LEAST THREE (3) SPED CENTERS IN BIG SCHOOL DIVISIONS FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS (CSN's), CREATING THE IMPLEMENTING MACHINERY THEREOF, PROVIDINGGUIDELINES FOR GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE AND OTHER INCENTIVES AND SUPPORT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is hereby declared the policy of the State to protect and promote the rights of children with special needs (CSN's) to quality education and to take appropriate steps to male such education accessible to them.  The State recognizes their vital role in national development and that finding solutions to their problems forms an integral part of national development strategies. It is also the policy of the State to give full support for their welfare and development to ensure their full integration to society as well as to facilitate their active participation in the affairs of the State. Towards this end and also pursuant to the mandate stated in Section 13 of Article II, Sec. 13 of Article XIII of the 1987 Constitution, Sec. 11-2, pars. 1 and 3 of Article XIV, Art. 3 of P.D. 603 and Sections 12-14 of R.A. 7277, the State shall institutionaliz e an adequate and relevant educational program for every child with special needs through the establishment of SPED Centers and of

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209 AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, THEREBY LIMITING MARRIAGE TO NATURAL BORN MALES AND NATURAL BORN FEMALES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Due to recent developments in the field of medicine, science and technology, it is now possible to alter or altogether change a person's sexual organ to make it appear as that of the opposite sex. A man can now change his penis into a vagina, and for a woman, vise versa. With this, we have directly challenged the laws of God, the laws of nature and even the laws of man. Recently, a celebrated case involving a marriage between a man who had a sex change operation with another man broke grounds in Philippine law.  This bill seeks to amend the Family Code to prohibit such marriages.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT OFFICE IN EVERY POLITICAL DISTRICT IN THE PHILIPPINES, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The district Members of the House of Representatives , as distinguished from those from the party-list, represent a definite political subdivision - the District. He is a local leader, inasmuch as he represents the interests of his constituents in the halls of congress and before departments and agencies of government. But he is also a national stakeholder, in that, in performing his duties he is not limited to promoting only parochial concerns and can take up issues and causes thataffect other localities or the entire country as well. With all these concerns on his burden, it is not surprising that the Congressman is, perhaps, the most visited public official, especially when he is in his district.

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SUBSECTION 3, ARTICLE 335 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES(RE: RAPE OF CHILDREN UNDER 12 YRS. OLD)
rows.abstract: The proposed amendment deals with WHEN AND HOW RAPE IS COMMITTED. The following circumstance is the subject of said amendment: When the woman is under twelve years of age, even though neither of the circumstances mentioned in the two next precedingparagraphs shall be present[.]: PROVIDED, THAT THE WOMAN IS NOT A PROFESSIONAL PROSTITUTE, OTHERWISE THE PARENTS OR ANY PERSON IN CHARGE OR PROMOTES THE SEX ACTIVITIES OF SUCH WOMAN SHALL BE HELD LIABLE FOR RAPE UNDER THIS SUB-SECTION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-01

first_reading.comm_act: chge of cttee. ref'l from Revision of Laws as per J.69;p.69( May5-7,200 3)

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE AGE OF STATUTORY RAPE FROM TWELVE (12) TO SIXTEEN (16) YEARS OLD, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 335 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is true that children ranging between 1 to 12 years old are such at a vulnerable stage of life. However, rape continues to be in the uptrend and the records speak for itself.  In 1995 alone, rape accounts for 48% of all sexual abuse and, unmistakably, could have risen further. What strikes us is that majority of the victims were from 13 to 17 years old.  Thus, the proposed amendment: "Article 335. When and how rape is committed. Rape is committed by having carnal knowledge of a woman under any of the following circumstances: 1.  By using force or intimidation; 2. When the woman is deprived of reason or otherwise unconscious; and 3.  When the woman is under SIXTEEN (16) years of age or is demented."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-01

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE SHOWING OF TELEVISION ADVERTISEMENTS FEATURING SEX AND/OR VIOLENCE TO CHILDREN OF TENDER AGE
rows.abstract: "Television Advertisement Regulation Act of 2001."  The showing of film or movie advertisements or trailers on television depicting violence and/or sex shall be aired only at such times when children of formative years are not usually watching television. Violation of the provisions of this Act as well as the rules and regulations thereunder that Act shall be punished by a fine of not less than Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000.00) nor more than Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) or imprisonment of not less than one (1) year nor more than five (5) years or both at the discretion of the Court.

It proposes that the amount of loans granted by banks and other financial institutions be based on audited financial statements that have been certified by theBureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) as the same set submitted to them.  This scheme encourages borrowers to declare their true income so that they can avail of bigger loan amounts. To fully implement the aforesaid guiding principles of decentralizatio n, the accompanying bill seeks to grant more powers to local government officials, specifically the appointment of treasurer, assistant treasurer, the secretary to the sanggunian and employees in the offices of the vice-governor, provincial board member, vice mayor and councilors.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE SALE OF TICKETS AND COLLECTION OF CONTRIBUTIONS FROM TEACHERS AND STUDENTS, SOLICITATION IN ANY FORM, AND/OR ANY SIMILAR FUND-RAISING ACTIVITY, IN ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY PUBLIC SCHOOLS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONSTHEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

rows.abstract: The sale of tickets and collection of contributions and/or solicitation in any form by any person or persons, whether voluntary or otherwise, from teachers and students in public elementary and secondary schools at any time of the school year are prohibited: Provided, That this prohibitiion shall not cover voluntary fees in the Red Cross, Girl Scouts of the Philippines and Boy Scouts of the Philippines, membership fees and annual dues of members of Parents-Teacher s Association (PTA), as well as voluntary contributions for projects of the PTA for the benefit of the school and projects of the student organizations.

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE LAUNDERING OF MONETARY INSTRUMENTS, AUTHORIZING THE EXAMINATION OF BANK RECORDS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The need for the enactment of a statute to check the problem posed by the laundering of money used for illegal activities is a must.  In particular, the need has been recognized in regard to the drugs menace, hence, this response, in a common effortas we march in step with the rest of the civilized world in confronting a universal problem.  Such dirty money, as it were, must be interdicted everywhere and not given any harbor of hospitality anywhere. Laundering will be criminalized. The authorities, particularly the Ombudsman and the Secretaries of Justice and Finance and the Central Bank Governor will also be authorized to examine the bank records or accounts of laundering suspects or defendants under certain conditions.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03083

rows.abstract: Rationale:  To achieve the goal of rehabilitating the real estate industry, it is imperative that the real estate industry be provided with ample assistance and incentives, including tax measures more conducive to greater activity in the real estatemarket. It is for this reason that this bill proposes to reduce the amount of value-added tax imposed on real estate transactions in order to bring prices of real estate to levels more attractive to the end consumer.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE MANDATE ON THE INTERCONNECTION BETWEEN AND AMONG PUBLIC TELECOMMUNICATI ONS ENTITIES, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The telephone industry consisting of landlines and cellular phone has been plagued by many problems, most severe of which is the failure for a phone company to gain access to another. Such failure of interconnection do not only provide inconvenience to individual subscribers but has affected business as well since inaccessibility will bring about waste of time, waste of labor, and loss of opportunity where dispatch and immediate action is necessary to communicate with another party or parties. The proposed bill opens the door for Congress to come out with a law that will impose severe monetary sanctions as well as criminal liability to erring telecoms companies who will now fail to interconnect after the NTC has determined the nnecessity for them to do so.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04418

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING NATIONAL HEALTH RESEARCH INSTITUTES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Philippine Medical Association (PMA) firmly believes that scientific medicine has not equal in health care delivery.  If we sincerely want to develop the medicinal potentials of our "7000 species of medicinal plants we should go for it with well organized and adequately funded scientific investigations. Therefore, the PMA proposes the creation of National Health Research Institutes to provide the key to unlock the active compounds from indigenous and non-indigenous sources and other health potentials obtainable in our country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-06

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE INSTITUTE OF PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  In addition to generic medicines, the Philippines has started to produce medicines using  native plants as raw materials. However, the pharmaceutical industry needs serious and continuous scientific research in order for the pharmaceutical industry to be competitive. This bill seeks to bring about such research to enable the country to establish its own pharmaceutical industry based on solid study and scientific research, so that the country will not be dependent on foreign sourcesfor its health well-being.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING CIGARETTE/CIGAR SMOKING IN PUBLIC PLACES AND PUBLIC CONVEYANCES AND IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Anti-Smoking Act of 2001." Rationale: It is hereby declared the policy of the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. It is also the policy of the State to safeguard public healthby discouraging cigarette/cigar smoking which has been determined to be harmful to the health of smokers and non-smokers alike.  To this end, the State shall regulate cigarette/cigar smoking.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

rows.abstract: This bill aims to :  (a) Rationalize the development and improvement of public health facilities, equipment and services in the country, both local and national, including health centers, clinics, laboratories, and hospitals; (b) Provide for a systematic prioritization and rational upgrading of national and locally-adminis tered health facilities, equipment and services as provided for by the proposed National Health Facilities Enhancement Plan.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: We must help invest money on developing an incentive-motiv ated and performance-dri ven health care system that will produce maximum efficiency in the provision of quality health services. We must appropriate money that ensures maximum return for our spending in terms of health benefits. When enacted, this bill will breathe life to this proposal. The National Health Service Delivery Enhancement Fund is hereby established. The fund shall institute an efficient, sustainable and equitable health care delivery system by providing incentives to the different health service providers.

rows.abstract: "Philippine Medical Act of 2001." This proposed measure shall govern the: (a) the standardization , upgrading, and regulation of medicine courses including internship training; (b) the examination for registration and licensure of Physicians; (c) the supervision, control and regulation of the practice of medicine; (d) the integration of the medical profession; and (e) the development of the professional competence of physicians through continuing professional education in accordance with the guidelines set by the Professional Regulation Commission.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04729

rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR ILLEGAL GAMBLING
rows.abstract: This bill enumerates what are considered UNAUTHORIZED games of chance.  The bill, likewise, imposes stiffer penalties to maintainers, financiers, employees and protectors of illegal gambling. Previous measures only impose either a fine or imprisonment. This measure proposes both fines and imprisonment as penalties for the violations of this act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REVERTING TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT THE DISCHARGE OF BASIC HEALTH SERVICES DEVOLVED TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUs) AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: "Renationalizat ion of Devolved Health Services and Facilities Act." The objectives of this Act are: a) To prevent the further deterioration of government health services and facilities brought about by devolution; b) to provide essential health services to the people, especially the sick, the poor and marginalized sector of society; c) to improve and uplift the morale, social and economic well-being of devolved health workers; and d) to develop a professional health manpower that is responsiveto the people's health needs and problems.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF PLUMBING ENGINEERING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Some forty years ago, 1955, Congress enacted R.A. 1378, otherwise known as the Plumbing Law, which regulates the trade of master plumbers. High School graduates with five years plumbing experience used to dominate the trade.  With the advent of high rise buildings their numbers are dingling but sustaining. Master Plumbers with engineering expertise are coming about. Since then the law has become outmoded with provisions that do not harmonize with the times.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROFESSIONALIZI NG THE GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTING SERVICE TO SERVE AS A TOOL FOR EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF GOVERNMENT RESOURCES, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTANCY OFFICE UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF BUDGET AND MANAGEMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Government Accounting Act of 1998."  All government transactions shall be properly documented, recorded, classified and interpreted into meaningful data; and communicated on a timely basis to fiscal authorities concerned so that the information generated therefrom can be made useful for economic analysis, policy formulation and decision-making purposes. The responsibility to document and record faithfully said transaction should rest with government accountants.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TAX INCENTIVES TO BROADCAST AND PRINT MEDIA DEVOTING AIR TIME AND SPACE TO EDUCATION, AS WELL AS, TO SPONSORS SUPPORTING SUCH PROGRAMS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Admittedly, media is an effective alternate vehicle to deliver educational services to our population. In this context, every Filipino can be extended educational services beyond the four corners of the classroom and in the comfort of their homes. Cognizant of the problem being encountered by the media industry and recognizing its importance to the present educational program, this bill grants tax incentives to media programs and publications, as well as, to their respective advertisers and sponsors, with educational thrust.  It is hoped that the measures contained in this bill will alleviate the economic plight of the media industry as a whole and shall become an effective tool in the success of the national educational programm.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM TAXATION ALL DONATIONS, GRANTS OR GIFTS TO NON-STOCK AND NON-PROFIT EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract: Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, all monetary contributions and the equivalent monetary value of properties donated, granted or bestowed to non-stock and non-profit institutions are tax-exempt and deductible from the taxable income of the donor: Provided, That such donations, grants, endowments or contributions shall be used actually, direclty, and exclusively for the primary educational purposes of the recipient: Provided, further, That not more than twenty-five (25) percent of the donations, grants, endowments or contributions shall be used for administrative purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-06
